commits.edited_message:
escape: use hex-pair lookup and classify unreserved bytes

Copy precomputed uppercase hex pairs instead of looking up each digit separately. Use an explicit RFC 3986 unreserved predicate for emission so decoding and escaping no longer share one classification.

Mark exclamation marks as valid non-hex literals in the shared table while preserving the existing stricter public escape output.

Add coverage for all 256 byte values, checking exact encoded output and round-trip decoding.

Closes #23021

tidy-up: null-terminator, NUL byte

Minor terminology cleanup across the tree. Also size curl_easy_escape() output exactly from its escape table.

Closes #23201

coupling: The first commit changes the shared hextable entry for "!" to a literal marker, but simultaneously moves public escape emission to an explicit RFC 3986 unreserved predicate that still escapes "!"; public behavior is unchanged and that commit is safe alone. The later commit replaces the conservative three-byte allocation with exact sizing based on hextable. Applied to the original tree, hextable and the writer agree, so that commit is also safe alone. When composed, the size pass treats "!" as one byte while the emission path writes three bytes, so an all-"!" public curl_easy_escape() input overflows the exactly sized heap buffer. The safe invariant is the agreement of two classifiers introduced in different commits; a correct fix must reason across both the table change and the new size pass rather than trusting either classification source in isolation.
